description:
## Goal

Produce a written audit of every Hash/Array/Channel in code paths
that run for the lifetime of the process. For each, document:
- The cap (if any)
- The eviction strategy
- What happens when the cap is hit
- Whether retention is measured in the memory log

## Scope

- All @@class_vars and @instance_vars in src/websocket/,
  src/services/, src/fetcher/, src/infrastructure/.
- All Hash/Array/Channel literals in those files.
- Skip short-lived locals and request-scoped state.

## Output

A new file at docs/memory-audit.md (or a long comment in
src/infrastructure/actor.cr if docs/ is not the right place)
with a table of structure | cap | eviction | measured? |
action-needed?.

The audit should also call out:
- AppStateService.@memory_history (cap 500, OK)
- AppStateService.@current (one snapshot, OK but verify
  copy_with does not retain old arrays)
- EventBroadcaster.@@client_history (cap 1000, OK)
- RateLimiter.@@allowed_cache (cap 256, OK)
- FaviconCache.@@cache + @@access_order (cap 200, OK)
- FaviconActor.@client_pool (uncapped — task 2)
- SocketManager.@connections (capped by MAX_CONNECTIONS, OK
  but cleanup gap is task 3)
- StringIntern.@@pool (cap 10000, see task on retention)

## Acceptance

- docs/memory-audit.md exists with the table.
- Each row links to the source file and line range.
- Each "action-needed" row links to the child task that
  addresses it.
title: Audit all unbounded data structures in long-lived paths
